summary.headline: Viceroy Hotels Q2 FY27 consolidated total income rose 53% to Rs 48.8 crore and EBITDA rose 46% to Rs 12.9 crore, with combined occupancy at 79.2%.
summary.overview: Consolidated total income for Q2 FY27 was Rs 48.8 crore, up 53% YoY, and EBITDA was Rs 12.9 crore, up 46%, at a 26.7% margin. H1 total income grew 61% to Rs 94 crore and H1 PAT rose 171% to Rs 3.7 crore. Quoteyard's 158 rooms returned to service after phase one, lifting combined occupancy, while the Marriott convention centre stayed offline for phase two renovation, costing about Rs 2 crore of EBITDA per quarter. The Rs 105.8 crore rights issue closed and about Rs 80.2 crore of debt was repaid in early October, leaving about Rs 182 crore of borrowings.

financial_highlights.change: +46% YoY vs Rs 3.8 crore (as stated; base figure appears inconsistent with margin); +9% QoQ
+171% vs Rs 1.4 crore in H1 FY26
vs Rs 19.4 crore earlier, mainly rights issue proceeds
Loan tenure 10 to 12 years; borrowings Rs 243.8 crore at end H1, Rs 182 crore after October repayment

segments.name: Marriott + Quoteyard combined
segments.commentary: Combined occupancy 79.2% in Q2 (vs 56.9% a year earlier), ADR Rs 6,650 (flat YoY, up 9% QoQ), RevPAR Rs 5,272 (+39%). Room revenue grew 39% to Rs 22.5 crore; F&B revenue was Rs 22.7 crore for H1, down 5%.

segments.name: Quoteyard
segments.commentary: Occupancy 87.4% (vs 31.5% last year), RevPAR Rs 5,711 (2.2x YoY). Improvement attributed to 158 rooms back in service after phase one; HAYU rooftop restaurant opened in August.

segments.name: Marriott
segments.commentary: Occupancy 74.5% (vs 71%), ADR Rs 6,738 (+1.8%), RevPAR Rs 5,022 (+6.3%). Convention centre offline since start of phase two; banqueting revenue Rs 10.8 crore in Q2, down 20% YoY (Rs 13.5 crore base).

segments.name: Executive apartments (Gachibowli)
segments.commentary: Q2 room revenue Rs 9.3 crore (+17%), F&B Rs 3.5 crore (+18%). Occupancy 88% (84% last year), ADR Rs 15,337 (+12%), RevPAR Rs 13,461 (+17%). H1 room revenue Rs 17.8 crore (+19%) at 91% occupancy.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the Marriott convention centre (expanded to 20,000 sq ft across three banquet halls) to reopen by end-December 2026; ramp-up to full occupancy expected in about 9 months, by Q3 FY28.
Management targets EBITDA margin of about 40% in the near term and a long-term range of 40% once renovation is complete (as transcribed; figure is unclear in the transcript).
Executive apartments Q3-Q4 YoY room revenue growth expected at 10-12%, per management.
Interest cost expected to fall: about Rs 8.8 crore for the next six months and about Rs 10.5 crore for the following full year, per management.
Marriott room renovation (295 rooms) moves to phase three, with work starting April 2027 and completion in FY28; complex to reach ADR of Rs 9,000-9,500 in FY28-FY29.
Renovation budget reaffirmed at about Rs 110-115 crore for the convention centre; Marriott room upgrade budget held at about Rs 40 crore.
Rs 25 crore of rights-issue proceeds retained for capex (convention centre), and daily operations.
capex_capacity: Quoteyard phase one (158 rooms) complete; HAYU rooftop restaurant opened in August 2026.
Marriott convention centre phase two: expansion to 20,000 sq ft across three banquet halls, on track for end-December 2026 completion; budget about Rs 110-115 crore.
Marriott phase three: 295 rooms, restaurants and lobbies, planned for FY28 starting April 2027; executives said rooms renovation will be sequenced with convention centre work.

Proposed 200-key Courtyard hotel at Mahapur in Hyderabad: permission in process, construction expected in next financial year (FY28). Combined complex of about 500 rooms once convention centre reopens.
demand_pricing: Management said Hyderabad demand is driven by GCC leasing, with the city accounting for about 37% of July-September GCC leasing; industry room rates rose in double digits by September.
Quoteyard rates trail Marriott; management said Marriott ADR should be about 5-7% above Quoteyard in the long run; newer rooms sell 25-40% above older rooms.
Foreign mix: Marriott and Quoteyard about 25% domestic and 15% foreign; executive apartments 20-30% foreign. Q3-Q4 has higher foreign demand.
Q1 was hit by West Asia conflict; business paused in Q1 returned in Q2. Q2 also benefited from a soft base.

qa_highlights.question: Why were executive apartments not in last year's base, and what is organic growth for the two hotels?
qa_highlights.answer: For the two hotels alone, room and F&B revenue grew about 12%, with rooms up 39% and F&B down 20%. The banqueting loss is about Rs 2 crore per quarter. Management said Q3-Q4 YoY growth at executive apartments is expected at 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is executive apartment ADR (Rs 15,337) below Q4 FY26 levels, and how is occupancy being prioritised?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1-Q2 strategy prioritised occupancy over rate, while Q3-Q4 prioritises rate because demand is seasonally stronger.

qa_highlights.question: Was the rights issue mainly to meet minimum public shareholding, and will there be further dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the issue was to meet the 75% public shareholding requirement, while debt was reduced. Promoter holding fell from 84.11% to 74.03%. Management does not expect further dilution.

qa_highlights.question: Why does Quoteyard RevPAR exceed Marriott's, and what is the Marriott target after renovation?
qa_highlights.answer: Quoteyard is smaller and fully renovated, and Marriott lacks a convention centre during renovation. Marriott is expected to run about 5-10% above Quoteyard ADR once the entire renovation is complete.

qa_highlights.question: How much of EBITDA improvement came from Courtyard, and how do the two Hyderabad properties share resources?
qa_highlights.answer: The full EBITDA improvement was from Quoteyard (Courtyard). The two properties will share a management team and back-office facilities like laundry.

qa_highlights.question: How much debt has been repaid since 30 September, and how will the remaining cash be used?
qa_highlights.answer: Rs 80.2 crore was repaid in early October 2026. The remaining funds are earmarked for capex (convention centre) and daily operations.

qa_highlights.question: What is the convention centre's expected revenue and payback?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ramp-up is half the usual 18 months for a greenfield project, reaching full throttle in about 9 months. Payback is expected in 13-24 months.

risks_watch: Convention centre reopening slated for end-December 2026; any slippage delays the high-margin banquet and wedding revenue.
F&B revenue fell 5% in H1 while convention centre is offline; management expects a return to growth only after reopening.
Quoteyard ADR fell about 4% in H1 and Marriott ADR rose only about 2% in Q2, so the rate gap to Marriott persists until renovation completes.
Shareholding: promoter holding fell to 74.03%; management says no further dilution planned.
Goodwill of Rs 38.6 crore from the acquisition of an entity; management says no impairment is expected given current performance.
Distressed and brownfield acquisitions are being sought, but management said few good deals are currently available.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the Quoteyard and executive apartment recovery, with specific numbers. Cautious on the Marriott convention centre (offline until end-December) and on the rate gap to Marriott. Several answers were loosely worded, and some Q&A figures (for example the ADR and margin references) were inconsistent, so they should be verified against the filing.
key_quotes: If I had to sum up this quarter in one line, it is the quarter in which the work we have put into our hotels over the last two years has started to show clearly in our numbers even with our convention centre at Marriott closed for elevation.
And to the question many of you asked last quarter whether rates would follow occupancy. I am happy to say they have started to.
With the RDA raising the repo rate in October for the first time since 2023, easily reducing debt is the right use of this capital.

adds.what: Marriott convention centre phase two: expansion to 20,000 sq ft across three banquet halls
Marriott phase three: 295-room renovation, restaurants and lobbies (upgrade, not net new rooms)
Proposed 200-key Courtyard hotel at Mahapur, Hyderabad

growth.why: Management guides H1 growth of 61% (Q2 +53%) backed by Quoteyard's 158 rooms back in service and industry rate increases, with the Marriott convention centre (Rs 110-115 cr capex) due to reopen end-December 2026 and a 200-key Mahapur hotel planned for FY28; the convention-centre reopening is specific, while the margin and ADR targets are less clearly supported.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose to 26.7% in Q2 from 26.3% in Q1 and H1 margin is 26.5% (+221 bps YoY); management targets about 40% long term once the convention centre reopens, though the 30% vs 40% near-term figure is inconsistent in the brief.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Marriott convention centre (20,000 sq ft, three banquet halls, Rs 110-115 crore) is on track to reopen by end-December 2026; Quoteyard's 158 rooms are already back in service; Mahapur 200-key Courtyard is only planned for FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Combined occupancy reached 79.2% in Q2 vs 56.9% a year ago, executive apartments are guided to 10-12% room revenue growth in Q3-Q4, and the convention centre adds banquet volume from end-December.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Combined occupancy of 79.2% is near the 80% threshold, and the Mahapur 200-key Courtyard is in permission with construction expected in FY28 (approval process under way, no firm date given).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: H1 total income grew 61% and Q2 grew 53% YoY, with Q3-Q4 seasonally stronger for foreign demand and executive apartments guided at 10-12%, but the convention centre is not yet reopened and the management guidance is not explicitly raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Any slippage in the end-December 2026 convention centre reopening would delay high-margin banquet revenue that is currently costing about Rs 2 crore of EBITDA per quarter, and banqueting revenue fell 20% YoY to Rs 10.8 crore in Q2.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The HAYU rooftop restaurant opened in August 2026 and the convention centre reopens end-December 2026 as an expanded 20,000 sq ft venue, though no new product beyond these is named.

rows.label: Debt cut after rights issue
rows.why: Rs 80.2 crore repaid in early October 2026 takes borrowings from Rs 243.8 crore to about Rs 182 crore, with interest cost guided to fall to about Rs 8.8 crore for the next six months.

rows.label: Marriott rate uplift after renovation
rows.why: Management targets complex ADR of Rs 9,000-9,500 in FY28-FY29, against Marriott ADR of Rs 6,738 in Q2 (+1.8% YoY), so this depends on phase three renovation starting April 2027.

rows.label: Marriott phase three room renovation
rows.why: The 295-room renovation (budget about Rs 40 crore) is approved with work starting April 2027 and completion in FY28, which will take rooms out of service during the ramp.

tone.note: Management was confident on the Quoteyard and executive apartment recovery and on the convention centre reopening by end-December, but cautious on the Marriott rate gap and banquet loss; analysts pushed on the ADR and margin figures, which the brief flags as inconsistent.
